source_text: Neque exhibeatis membra vestra arma iniquitatis peccato, sed exhibete vos Deo, tamquam ex mortuis viventes, et membra vestra arma iustitiae Deo. Peccatum enim in vobis non dominatur; non enim sub lege estis, sed sub gratia [n387] . Eo, inquit, debetis servire Deo fidelius, quo etiam liberalius; peccatum quippe dominabatur vobis, cum reatuum impendebat ultio; postea autem quam gratia Dei beneficia consecuti estis et depositis reatuum ponderibus respirastis, ingenuo pudore commoniti debetis gratiam referre medicanti.
pass_a_gloss: Nor exhibit your members as arms of iniquity to sin, but exhibit yourselves to God, as living from the dead, and your members as arms of justice to God. For sin does not dominate in you; for you are not under the law, but under grace. By this, he says, you ought to serve God more faithfully, by which also more liberally; for sin was dominating you, when a vengeance of reatus was hanging over; but afterward, when you obtained the benefits of the grace of God and, the weights of reatus having been laid down, you breathed, warned by a freeborn shame you ought to bring back thanks to the one healing.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: ‘Do not present your members as weapons of injustice to sin, but present yourselves to God as people alive from the dead, and your members as weapons of righteousness to God. For sin does not rule over you: you are not under law but under grace’ (Romans 6:13–14). You should, he says, serve God more faithfully because you do so more freely. Sin ruled over you when punishment for guilt hung over you. But after you received the benefits of God’s grace and breathed freely with the weight of your guilt laid down, a free person’s sense of honor should prompt you to show gratitude to your healer.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)
